In one dimension the two halfspaces through j are the two closed tails; both include the atom at j. For h>j the left index is off support. For 1≤h≤j monotonicity and nonnegative-index zero extension make w_(j+h) the smaller weight. This gives exactly one contribution per reflected pair and the displayed prefix-sum difference.

Adding the reflected sum to both depth branches gives the displayed formula. At 0≤j<N the second branch changes by −w_j−w_(j+1)+w_(2j+1)+w_(2j+2)≤0. The paired inequalities follow from j≤2j+1 and j+1≤2j+2, even if the latter indices exceed N. The first branch is nondecreasing.

A weak superlevel is the intersection of a terminal and an initial interval. Reversal j↦N−j swaps the closed tails and preserves the reflected sum. N=0, all zero weights, plateaus, and empty or full superlevels fit these arguments.

In a finite nonempty family the largest lower endpoint and smallest upper endpoint are attained. If they come from different intervals, pairwise intersection gives the desired order. If they come from the same interval, its nonemptiness does. The largest lower endpoint is then a common integer anchor.
Cross-checked the identities, reflected indexing and superlevel intervals on 1,286 monotone integer profiles with N≤7 and weights in {0,1,2,3,4}.
